# hole-and-prefix-ownership: a token inside a structural position a value reader accepts.
# a python f-string hole keeps its literal text (a quoted string with escaped quotes, a format
# spec, the spec of a nested replacement field), a hole off a python file is literal data, a shell
# reads `b"x"<word>` as one word, and a misread key or a `&&` command word gives the token back
# when it is no code of words.
# format: <rule id> TAB <line>.
generic-high-entropy-value	value=f"{'a\'{S32}\'b'}"
generic-high-entropy-value	value=f"{'\'{S32}\''}"
generic-high-entropy-value	value=f"{name:{S32}}"
generic-high-entropy-value	value=f"{name!r:{S40}}"
generic-high-entropy-value	value = f"{x:{y}{S32}}"
generic-high-entropy-value	value = f"{name.label:{S36}}"
generic-high-entropy-value	value = f"{lookup('{S36}')}"
generic-high-entropy-value	VALUE=f"{{S32}}"
generic-high-entropy-value	VALUE=b"short"{S32}
generic-high-entropy-value	VALUE=r"short"{S32}
generic-high-entropy-value	VALUE=f"short"{S32}
generic-high-entropy-value	VALUE=b""{S32}
generic-high-entropy-value	export VALUE=rb'x'{S36}
generic-high-entropy-value	VALUE=u8"x"{S40}
generic-high-entropy-value	KEY=short&&{S32}
generic-high-entropy-value	tr -d '[[:alnum:]]{S32}'
generic-high-entropy-value	printf 'a\n: {S32}'
generic-high-entropy-value	Acquire::{S32}=true
generic-high-entropy-value	X::{S40}
